perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s available perspective:

- I am a plumber. Gary Guo is my close, long-time friend; we met in middle school and have relied on each other for emotional and professional support. Gary is a doctor.
- I noticed Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. I was concerned about his health.
- I invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat to relax and gain perspective. I heard Gary say he appreciated my concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, I observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. I suspected his overworking was about more than professional obligations.
- I confronted Gary, telling him that since we’d been friends since middle school, he could tell me anything, and that I was there to help, not judge. I heard him say it was complicated and he didn’t want to burden me.
- Gary opened up to me about pressures managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing. I felt relief and empathy.
- I suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. I heard Gary agree, saying he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, I regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges. I heard him say things were better, he was less overwhelmed thanks to my help, and he had time for a movie last weekend. I felt hopeful and proud and continued encouraging him.
- After a year, I saw Gary as capable of managing on his own, felt satisfied and happy for him, and decided to step back. I told him I’m always a call away and that he’s got this. He thanked me, said he couldn’t have done it without my support, and said he felt more in control.
